To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

repeated centrifugation of a feed extract after detergent treatment did not significantly increase recovery of bacteria, and that the bacterial populations recovered from the feed extracts were significantly correlated to the bacterial populations from the original feeds.

repeated centrifugation after extraction of feed with a detergent solution resulted in recovery of bacterial populations from feeds that are significantly correlated with the original populations in the feed, but the recovery is no more than 1/10th of the original populations in fresh feeds and less than 1/1000th of the original bacterial populations in feeds held in long term cold storage.
the recovery of bacterial populations from fresh and stored feed is poor after repeated centrifugation of the feed extract, but the recovery of bacterial population from feed extracts is good.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a rapid method for the enumeration of bacteria in animal feed.
the use of a detergent-based solution and repeated centrifugation as a method to remove non-microbial feed constituents from animal feeds prior to bacterial population enumeration.
the development of a new methodology to recover bacteria from animal feeds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a detergent solution combined with repeated extraction by centrifugation is not an efficient means of extracting bacteria from animal feeds.
the recovery of bacterial populations from animal feeds by repeated extraction and centrifugation after treatment with a detergent-based extraction solution is unreliable.
repeated centrifugation of feed samples exposed to detergent-based solutions resulted in recoveries of bacterial populations generally no more than about 10% of those in the original feed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
repeated centrifugation after detergent extraction of feeds is not an appropriate method for enumerating bacteria from feeds.
the recovery of heterotrophic bacteria from feed extracts was generally poor, but was correlated with the heterotrophic bacterial populations from the feed and from feed extracts.
a single centrifugation step after exposure to a liquid detergent-based solution was sufficient for the recovery of bacterial populations in animal feeds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
repeated centrifugation after extraction with a liquid detergent solution is not a viable method of extracting bacterial populations from animal feeds.
repeated centrifugation after detergent exposure may not be a suitable method for recovery of bacteria from feeds, particularly feeds that have been stored for extended periods.
a simple extraction step with repeated centrifugations does not appear to be a viable method for recovery of the majority of the microbial population present in feed samples.
